title: Matching monomial coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with entries in $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For a permutation $\tau$ of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, suppose $A_{i,\tau(i)}=\mathrm{true}$ for every $i$. In the determinant of the polynomial matrix whose $(i,j)$ entry is the indeterminate $X_{i,j}$ when $A_{i,j}=\mathrm{true}$ and zero otherwise, the coefficient of $\prod_i X_{i,\tau(i)}$ is the sign of $\tau$, viewed as an element of $R$.
hypotheses_covered: $\tau$ is a permutation of the indices
